title: Boss: port the legacy suite to xUnit v3
summary: The upgrade branch does not compile. Port a v2 suite to v3, turn copy-pasted money tests into a typed table, and share one expensive fixture across two classes.

steps.title: Ticket PLAT-77: move the blog service to xUnit v3
body: The platform team bumped the test packages from `xunit` 2.9 to `xunit.v3`. The build log of the upgrade branch:
SlugTests.cs(1,7): error CS0246: The type or namespace name 'Abstractions' does not exist in the namespace 'Xunit'
SlugTests.cs(3,28): error CS0738: 'SlugFixture' does not implement interface member 'IAsyncLifetime.InitializeAsync()'.
'SlugFixture.InitializeAsync()' cannot implement 'IAsyncLifetime.InitializeAsync()' because it does not have the
SlugTests.cs(3,28): error CS0738: 'SlugFixture' does not implement interface member 'IAsyncDisposable.DisposeAsync()'. ...
The v2 to v3 changes that bite most suites:
| `using Xunit.Abstractions;` for `ITestOutputHelper` | it lives in `Xunit`, and the old package is gone |
| `IAsyncLifetime` with `Task InitializeAsync()` / `Task DisposeAsync()` | `ValueTask` for both (it now extends `IAsyncDisposable`) |
| a class library run by a VSTest adapter | an executable test project (`OutputType` Exe), run by MTP |
| `async void` tests tolerated | `async void` tests are not supported: return `Task` |
| `Skip` only as a fixed attribute | also `Assert.Skip(...)`, `SkipUnless`, explicit tests |
Fix the compile errors first, then check the suite still catches the bugs it used to.

steps.title: Port the suite to v3
prompt: This is the v2 suite from the branch. Make it compile and pass on xUnit v3 **without weakening it**: it runs against the real `Slug.From` and against six planted bugs, and it must still catch all of them.
`Slug.From` makes URL slugs: lower case, ASCII letters and digits, single dashes between words, no dash at either end, and it throws `ArgumentException` for a blank title.
starter: public void Makes_slugs(string title, string expected)
solution: public void Makes_slugs(string title, string expected)

target: else if (!dash && sb.Length > 0) { sb.Append('-'); dash = true; }

mutants.name: runs of punctuation make several dashes
a slug can start with a dash
a slug can end with a dash

forbid.message: No Xunit.Abstractions (it is a v2 package)

hints: Read the first error: `ITestOutputHelper` is in the `Xunit` namespace in v3, which every test file already has.
Delete the `using`, change both methods to return `ValueTask`, and return `ValueTask.CompletedTask`.
steps.explain: A port is done when the suite compiles, passes, and still catches what it caught before. Checking the last part (here with planted bugs) is what stops an upgrade from silently weakening a suite, for example by "fixing" a red test with `Skip`.

steps.title: Money parsing as a typed table
prompt: The payments team pasted 11 nearly identical facts for `Money.Parse`. Replace them with **two theories**. The code under test:
```csharp
using System.Globalization;
public readonly record struct Money(decimal Amount, string Currency)
public static Money Parse(string text)
var parts = text.Trim().Split(' ', StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries);
if (parts.Length != 2) throw new FormatException($"Expected \"<amount> <currency>\", got \"{text}\".");
if (!decimal.TryParse(parts[0], NumberStyles.Number, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, out var amount) || amount <= 0)
throw new FormatException($"Bad amount \"{parts[0]}\".");
var currency = parts[1];
if (currency.Length != 3 || !currency.All(char.IsAsciiLetterUpper)) throw new FormatException($"Bad currency \"{currency}\".");
return new Money(amount, currency);
Write `public class MoneyTests` with:
- `public static TheoryData<string, decimal, string> Valid` and a `[Theory]` with `[MemberData(nameof(Valid))]` that checks the amount and currency (`decimal` cannot go in `[InlineData]`);
- a `[Theory]` with `[InlineData]` rows of text that must throw `FormatException`.
At least **10** rows in all. Six planted bugs, including one that parses with the German culture and one that cannot read `1,234.56`.
starter: public void Parses_euros() => Assert.Equal(new Money(12.50m, "EUR"), Money.Parse("12.50 EUR"));
solution: public static TheoryData<string, decimal, string> Valid => new()
public void Parses_amount_and_currency(string text, decimal amount, string currency)

target: public readonly record struct Money(decimal Amount, string Currency)
if (!decimal.TryParse(parts[0], NumberStyles.Number, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, out var amount) || amount <= 0)

mutants.name: thousands separators are refused
mutants.hint: Add a valid row with a thousands separator, such as 1,234.56.

mutants.name: it parses with the German culture
two spaces in a row break parsing
mutants.hint: Add a valid row with two spaces between the amount and the currency.

hints: `public static TheoryData<string, decimal, string> Valid => new() { { "12.50 EUR", 12.50m, "EUR" }, ... };`
Each planted bug needs a row that shows it: `1,234.56 USD`, `3.10  CHF` (two spaces), `0 EUR`, `12.50 eur`, `12.50 EURO`.
German culture reads `12.50` as 1250: any valid row with a decimal point catches it, as long as you assert the amount.
steps.explain: Two tables read like the specification: what is accepted, what is refused. `TheoryData` keeps `decimal` as `decimal`, so no floating-point conversion sneaks into money tests.

steps.title: One fixture for two test classes
prompt: `PriceDb` from *Fixtures and test lifetime* is back (open it once per run, or it throws). This time two classes need it, `PriceTests` and `BasketTests`. A class fixture would open it once **per class**, which is twice.
Write:
1. `public sealed class PriceDbFixture : IAsyncLifetime` (as before);
2. a collection definition: `[CollectionDefinition("price db")] public class PriceDbCollection : ICollectionFixture<PriceDbFixture>;`
3. `PriceTests` and `BasketTests`, both marked `[Collection("price db")]` and taking the fixture in their constructor, with at least **four** tests between them.
`PriceDb` is the same as before: mug 8.00, tea 4.50, pot 24.00; `PriceOf` throws `KeyNotFoundException` for an unknown SKU; `Basket(params string[] skus)` adds them up.
starter: public PriceDb Db { get; private set; } = null!;
public async ValueTask InitializeAsync() => Db = await PriceDb.OpenAsync();
public async ValueTask DisposeAsync() => await Db.DisposeAsync();
solution: public PriceDb Db { get; private set; } = null!;
public async ValueTask InitializeAsync() => Db = await PriceDb.OpenAsync();
public async ValueTask DisposeAsync() => await Db.DisposeAsync();

target: throw new InvalidOperationException("PriceDb is expensive: open it once in a fixture, not in every test.");
public decimal PriceOf(string sku) => prices.TryGetValue(sku, out var p) ? p : throw new KeyNotFoundException(sku);
public decimal Basket(params string[] skus) => skus.Sum(PriceOf);

mutants.name: the basket drops its first item

require.message: Both test classes join the collection

hints: The starter fails because each `IClassFixture` makes its own fixture: the second one opens the database again.
A collection fixture is created once for every class in the collection. The definition class has no body: `public class PriceDbCollection : ICollectionFixture<PriceDbFixture>;`.
Remove `IClassFixture<...>` from both classes and put `[Collection("price db")]` on each; the constructor parameter stays.
steps.explain: Collection fixtures are how real suites share one database container or one test host across many classes. The price: classes in one collection never run in parallel with each other, which is usually what shared state needs anyway.
